question: As per the Indian Space Association (ISpA) in 2025, _____ satellites out of the approved 52-satellite constellation for the defence sector are expected to be built by the private sector
solution:
The Correct answer is __**31**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the **Indian Space Association (ISpA)**, by the year **2025**, out of the approved **52-satellite constellation** for the defence sector, **31 satellites** are expected to be built by the **private sector**.
 
• This marks a significant step towards the involvement of **private entities** in the development of India's space and defence-related technologies.
 
• The initiative supports the vision of **self-reliance (Atmanirbhar Bharat)** in the space sector, as promoted by the **Government of India**.
 
• Private sector participation is crucial in reducing the burden on public organizations like the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** and fostering **innovation** through competitive development.
 
• The 31 satellites are expected to cater to **defence-related communication, surveillance, and strategic needs**, strengthening India's national security infrastructure.
 
• This move aligns with the **space sector reforms** introduced in recent years, aiming to provide more opportunities to private players and startups in the space ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Private Sector Involvement in Space**__

 __
 
• Recently, the Government of India has introduced **policy reforms** to facilitate private sector participation in the space sector.
 
• Organizations like **IN-SPACe (Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Center)** have been established to promote and regulate private sector activities in space.
 
• Startups and private companies like **Skyroot Aerospace, Agnikul Cosmos, and Pixxel** have emerged as key players in India's evolving space industry.
 
• The government also aims to commercialize space technology through its commercial arm, **NewSpace India Limited (NSIL)**.
 
 
 
• **Defence Space Applications**__
 
 
• Satellites play a vital role in **military communication, navigation, surveillance, and reconnaissance**.
 
• They provide critical information for **border security, disaster management, and strategic operations**.
 
• Examples of defence-oriented satellites include **RISAT (Radar Imaging Satellite)** and **GSAT series satellites**.
